I don't know anyone with a Chromebook, nor have I ever used one. I think I understand what market Google was going for but I'm curious who actually buys and uses them. Serious replies only please.
Chromebook owners, what do you use them for? What makes them better than laptops, conversely what features are missing? Do you recommend them to friends?

Remote Desktop!!!! Damnit! I bought one for my dad thinking that it would be better for him than his older laptop. Man was I wrong, the lack of Remote Desktop means there is no easy way I can help him unless I fly to his location.
Are there any other areas that the Chromebook falls short or excels?

To be honest, I haven't used one since I set that one up for my dad. But the time I spent on it I liked it very much. Obviously the lack of a CD ROM kind of bothered me a bit. But with digital content being the norm now I really don't see that as a huge problem. The device started up very quickly and it was excellent on battery life. That's about all I can tell you on it since it was soon sent to my dad.

Appreciate your comments, especially since there hasn't been a lot of responses.

My impression in general is that if you're looking for a Windows laptop replacement then a Chromebook may not be for you. But for light, on-line centric usage it's just the thing.

FWIW you can get 10" android tablets with attachable keyboards for less than $200 (delivered). Then run Splashtop Remote Desktop for remote access.
